text: Add dimension! I know it sounds weird and wasteful but it will make a big difference- take your logs on the side, and pull them towards the front of the house by one block. Then take more logs and place them on top of one log, and go across until you meet the other log. By this time you should be able to put your face against the planks, and have your head under (but not touching!) the logs. Do that all the way around. Then build the logs up and adjust the roof so that they cover the logs top. Add windows some windows on the front of the house and your done!

text: Add depth to your walls. Push things in or out a block to add depth. For example you can move those logs outwards. Never have a completely flat wall with one block type. Try to have 2 or 3 blocks of depth with features at multiple levels. Use a multitude of blocks. Blocks that have colour that complement each other work together. The most common palette is two colours that contrast or complement eachother and a variety of textures in both colours. For example wood and stone work together well well and using planks, logs, stripped wood for the brown colours and then stone, cobblestone, stone bricks and adesite for the grey colours. Use blocks that aren't cubes. Things like buttons, stairs, fences, wallls, ladders all add detail to your build. Make your layout interesting. For a house specifically experiment with different shaped room, amount of stories, the height of each stories, connections between rooms. Don't always stick to a grid for rooms. Add exterior features. If you have a flat wall with nothing maybe add a window that can have a planter box or a balcony area. Add a chimney or lightning rood to the roof. Anything you might expect to be attached to the outside of a building. Have a progression upwards. Usually this is done by adding a strip at the bottom of the walls. But having your building visually slightly change as it goes upwards is very good. Don't follow any of this strictly. But take what you can and use it. Happy building.
label: layout_tip

text: Layers on layers. Look at buildings in real life and other people builds, the main thing you will notice is that things aren’t just flat. Bring your corner pillars out diagonally one block and make a support truss going across connecting them(you can use stairs to make diagonal lines from the cross to the roof to put more detail), extend the roof to cover the extra space(real houses do this for drainage), add some flower boxes, windows with trapdoors around them for depth(spruce on either side looks like storm shudders), try different roof designs using a mix of slabs and stairs to end up with a shorter less peaked roof, throw a chimney up there somewhere with a campfire to make it look like you have a fire going inside. Minecraft has a ton of blocks to choose from, throw a bunch down and see how you like the pallet. Stone types make a strong looking roof but can look out of place if the house looks like it would collapse under the weight. Different wood types fit different places, darker woods look weathered like they are an exterior thing(but can absolutely work inside) while lighter woods like birch make a brighter more “welcoming” interior. The creativity goes as far as you will take it.
